qualitative.gate_2_reason: Discretionary big-ticket purchase deferrable in recessions; cyclical residential homebuilder exposed to mortgage rates and housing cycle.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 2 (REJECT). UK's largest volume housebuilder following the 2024 Barratt-Redrow merger. New home purchases are discretionary, big-ticket commitments that buyers defer during interest rate spikes and recessions. As a cyclical volume homebuilder exposed to UK mortgage rates, consumer affordability, and planning bottlenecks, it fails Munger's non-deferrable essential need standard.
qualitative.evidence: Barratt Redrow (formed via the £2.5B acquisition of Redrow by Barratt Developments in 2024) delivers ~14,000 homes annually across the UK. During the 2022-2024 rate shock, completions fell over 20% (Barratt standalone completions dropped from 17,206 in FY23 to 14,004 in FY24), operating margins collapsed from ~16-18% peak down to ~7-9%, and ROCE plummeted from ~25-30% in peak Help-to-Buy years to single digits (<8% in FY24). In addition, building safety and cladding remediation provisions exceed £600M cumulative. The merger adds integration execution risk and overheads to an already capital-intensive, cyclical volume builder model with no pricing power over mortgage rate swings.
